pairs.question: Num ille te nam novit?
pairs.derivation: Palaestrio asks whether the soldier knows Acroteleutium (num = expecting 'no'); she answers that he has never seen her. Answer cut at the first full stop after 'vidit'; what follows ('qui noverit me quis ego sim?') is a rhetorical follow-on elaboration, not part of the direct answer. Speaker labels (Pal., Acr.) dropped.

pairs.question: Quo pacto potis nupta et vidua esse eadem?
pairs.derivation: Pyrgopolinices asks how the same woman can be both married and widowed; Palaestrio answers (a young woman married to an old man). The question itself repeats 'nupta et vidua', so it is self-contained without importing the prior speaker's line. Speaker labels (Pyrg., Pal.) and the dangling inline verse numbers (964-965, 966) stripped; line-wrap artifact rejoined.

pairs.question: Qui tu scis eas adesse?
pairs.answer: Quia oculis meis vidi hic sororem esse eius.
pairs.derivation: Pyrgopolinices asks how Palaestrio knows the sister and mother are present; Palaestrio answers that he saw with his own eyes that her sister is here. Answer cut at the full stop after 'eius'; the referent of 'eas' is supplied by the answer itself ('sororem ... eius'). Speaker labels (Pyrg., Pal.) and inline verse number (1105) stripped.

pairs.question: Quin tua causa exegit virum ab se. Qui id facere potuit?
pairs.derivation: Milphidippa states the wife drove her husband off for Pyrgopolinices's sake; he asks how she could do that ('id'); Milphidippa answers that the house belongs to the wife by dowry. The setup sentence ('Quin tua causa exegit virum ab se') is kept verbatim and contiguous so 'id' has a referent. Speaker labels (Milph., Pyrg., Mil.) stripped; answer ends at first full stop, before 'Itane?/Ita pol.'
